set.st: Four men robbed the Wabeno State Bank of $32,000 in cash and negotiable securities on 15 July 1921 (first put at $27,000). The gang was Willis and Lawrence Lesperance of Oconto and Chalmers and "Frenchie" Yaeger of Green Bay. Willis Lesperance and one Yaeger were taken on 23 July and lodged at Crandon; Lawrence Lesperance and Chalmers Yaeger were caught at Chippewa Falls in August. Sentences of 25 years each at Crandon were reported in 1921; a jail-break attempt at Crandon followed in September 1921, and in 1922 Lawrence drew a year at Waupun as an accessory. By their confession they buried the loot in the woods some distance from Wabeno while posses were on their trail. In July 1922 Lawrence was brought from Waupun for a day-long search that found nothing. In August 1922 berry pickers found a weather-beaten touring car on an abandoned logging trail in the wilderness about 20 miles east of Wabeno, several miles west of Athelstane, and the search moved there. Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself. In 1928 a letter in the Capital Times said "no recovery was ever made"; Lesperance claimed the money was buried in the woods a short distance from Wabeno and staged fake show-the-spot trips. In August 1922 berry pickers found the rusted getaway car on an abandoned logging trail about 20 mi E of Wabeno and several miles W of Athelstane, in ground the earlier searches had not covered. Car spot is an inference; one dug-up empty cache was reported in 1921. (A rumored hiding place on the Chippewa River bank at Chippewa Falls, where the gang's weapons were found, is not pinned.) By July 1922 all but about $8,000 had been recovered; Lesperance, then serving a year at Waupun, was taken out by Sheriff Miller at the bank's expense for an all-day search and found nothing. The later 'never recovered' reports refer to that $8,000. In 1912 this was cut-over lumber-company land; the 1938 aerial shows brush, swamp strips and faint logging trails but cannot single out where the car was found. In June 1922 the sheriff brought robber Lesperance from Waupun to search the woods near Wabeno for the $8,000 he said was hidden in the underbrush; the Yaeger brothers were promised 10 years off if it was found. Nothing turned up. A second pin marks the 1921 search ground about 7 mi N of Wabeno. The chase ran south of Wabeno: on 16 July posses closed on Mountain (Oconto County), and on 19-20 July some 300 men besieged the gang in the Carter woods (Carter, about 3.5 miles SSE of Wabeno), where two deputies were shot before the gang broke out over the cutover.

In 1900 strangers came to Homer, six miles down the river from Winona, looking for money said to have been hidden in one of the caves near Homer by bandits who had held up a train. The man who knew the place was said to be in prison for life and to have told them where it was. Nothing was found. In October 1903 a Homer resident announced a systematic search. The amount is OCR-damaged ("$?,000"). Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself. Mar 1901: two Kentuckians searched Homer caves for $8,500 from a Milwaukee Road train robbery, told by a dying old man; Oct 1903: a Homer resident planned a systematic search for ~$6,000 hidden by train bandits, the one who knew the place being in prison for life. Independent listing: Homer Post Office (historical) [GNIS Post Office, Winona East]; Homer (MN gazetteer 1888: village, pop. 25, 5 listings). This confirms the place existed; the pin position still comes from the earlier source.

set.pl: Kuehn farmyard, NW part of the SW quarter of sec. 22, Sigel Township, Brown County, by the sec. 21/22 road (1905 atlas quarter; 1939 aerial farmyard)
